channel.title: The Forge — TRE Forged
channel.description: Practical, jargon-free personal finance guides from TRE Forged: budgeting, saving, debt payoff, and getting the most out of Forgenta.

item.title: The Monthly Money Review: A 30-Minute Habit That Changes Everything
item.description: Learn how to run a simple 30-minute monthly money review with this step-by-step checklist for tracking spending, savings, and debt in 2026.

item.title: The 15-Minute Subscription Audit That Saves You Hundreds
item.description: Learn how to find and cancel forgotten subscriptions in just 15 minutes with this step-by-step audit that can save you hundreds of dollars a year.

item.title: How to Check All Your Car's Fluids: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Learn where to find and how to check your car's oil, coolant, brake, power steering, transmission, and washer fluid in about 20 minutes.

item.title: How to Automate Your Finances So Saving Happens on Its Own
item.description: Learn how to automate bills, savings, and debt payments in 2026 so your money moves on schedule without relying on willpower or memory.

item.title: 20 Realistic Ways to Cut Your Monthly Expenses in 2026
item.description: 20 practical, no-extreme-frugality ways to lower your monthly bills, ranked from easy quick wins to bigger changes with the biggest payoff.

item.title: Sinking Funds Explained: The Budgeting Trick That Ends Money Surprises
item.description: Learn what sinking funds are, which budget categories need one, and how to set them up so irregular expenses never blow up your budget again.

item.title: How to Check Your Tire Pressure and Tread (And Why It Saves You Real Money)
item.description: Learn to check tire PSI and tread depth in minutes with a simple gauge and the penny test, and see how proper pressure saves fuel and extends tire life.

item.title: High-Yield Savings Accounts: What They Are and Why They Matter
item.description: Learn how high-yield savings accounts work, what to compare before opening one, and how they fit into a solid emergency fund plan in 2026.

item.title: Needs vs. Wants: How to Tell the Difference When It Matters
item.description: A practical framework for sorting needs from wants in your budget, with real edge cases like cars, subscriptions, and gym memberships.

item.title: How to Stop Living Paycheck to Paycheck: A Real-World Plan for 2026
item.description: Learn how to stop living paycheck to paycheck with a practical plan: find the leak in your spending, build a small buffer, and automate savings.

item.title: How to Actually Track Your Expenses (and Stick With It)
item.description: Learn the real methods for tracking expenses, why most people quit within weeks, and a simple system that actually sticks in 2026.

item.title: How Much Should You Really Have in an Emergency Fund?
item.description: Find out exactly how much emergency savings you need based on your life situation, plus the best places to keep your fund in 2026.

item.title: How to Replace Your Windshield Wiper Blades (The Easiest DIY Car Job You'll Ever Do)
item.description: Learn how to pick the right wiper blades, remove the old ones, and install new blades in minutes with this beginner-friendly, step-by-step DIY guide.

item.title: Zero-Based Budgeting: How to Give Every Dollar a Job (Without Burning Out)
item.description: A practical guide to zero-based budgeting for beginners, covering who it suits, how to set one up, and how to stick with it in 2026.

item.title: How to Save Money on Groceries Without Coupons
item.description: Cut your grocery bill in 2026 with meal planning, unit pricing, and waste reduction strategies that work better than clipping coupons.

item.title: How to Build an Emergency Fund (Even on a Tight Budget)
item.description: An emergency fund is the foundation of financial stability. Here's how much you need, where to keep it, and how to build one even when money is tight.

item.description: The 50/30/20 rule is the simplest way to budget your take-home pay. Here's exactly what counts as needs, wants, and savings — with real dollar examples.

item.title: How to Build Your First Budget in 2026 (Step-by-Step)
item.description: A beginner-friendly, step-by-step guide to building your first budget in 2026 — how to track income, sort expenses, pick a budgeting method, and actually stick to it.
